---
title: "Call for Contributions"
---


Across many scientific disciplines, meta-scientific research has driven substantial reform in the last decade — studies of replication failure, publication bias, and questionable research practices prompted replication initiatives, preregistration, and open data policies that have reshaped how empirical research is conducted and evaluated. Yet methodological research disciplines — disciplines that develop and evaluate the methods underlying empirical research (e.g., statistics, psychometrics, bioinformatics, methods in ecology, econometrics, or machine learning) — have received little  meta-scientific attention, and have yet to embrace similar reforms.


This is beginning to change. Across a number of methodological disciplines, researchers have started to investigate how methods are developed and evaluated in their own fields, and how this process could be improved. Yet these efforts remain largely isolated — with little cross-disciplinary exchange and no shared vocabulary for thinking about rigor in methods research. The **1st Interdisciplinary Symposium on Meta Science for Methods Research** aims to change this, by bringing these communities together for the first time to share insights, build common ground, and collectively advance meta science for methods research.

We invite contributions that advance our understanding of methods research as a scientific object in its own right — how methods are developed, evaluated, and how this process can be improved. Topics of interest include, but are not limited to:

- Meta-scientific studies of methods research. For example, empirical investigations into reporting practices of simulation or benchmarking studies.

- Tools for improving methods research. For example, tools to run standardized benchmarks of computational methods.

- Perspectives on improving rigor in methods research. For example, evaluations of whether preregistration of simulation or benchmarking studies is or is not worthwile.

- TODO: add more topics?

Contributions can take the form of a poster or a 20-minute presentation (including  discussion). The scientific committee will evaluate all submissions and inform about acceptance within four weeks after the deadline.
